name: VQAonline
description: The first fully authentic Visual Question Answering (VQA) dataset sourced from online question answering community forums (Stack Exchange). Contains visual questions, images, context, and answers validated by those who asked the questions. Covers 105 diverse topics across five super-categories: culture & recreation, life & arts, science, professional, and business.
creator: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, Danna Gurari
publisher: University of Texas at Austin, Microsoft, University of Colorado Boulder
citeAs: Chen, C., Liu, M., Codella, N., Li, Y., Yuan, L., & Gurari, D. (2024). Fully Authentic Visual Question Answering Dataset from Online Communities. arXiv:2311.15562v4 [cs.CV]
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected by scraping publicly-available data from the Stack Exchange online question-answering platform spanning from August 2010 to November 2022. Each example contains a natural language question (collected as post 'title'), a natural language context (collected via 'body' text entry field), an image (collected as URL link), and at least one answer. Individuals who posted visual questions could mark which answer was the 'accepted answer'; only examples with accepted answers were included.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Stack Exchange platform data from 105 topical sites across five super-categories: 46 about culture & recreation, 25 about life & arts, 24 about science, 7 about being professional, and 3 about business. Data sourced from publicly-available Stack Exchange archive.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two filtering steps were conducted: (1) Removed low-quality VQAs based on Stack Exchange's voting feature - excluded visual questions with scores 0 or less for either the question or answer. (2) Excluded visual questions with multiple images (e.g., GIF) or with visual answers. Final dataset contains 64,696 VQAs after filtering and removing examples where images could not be downloaded. All images were converted to png format for consistency.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Answers were provided by Stack Exchange community members and validated by the individuals who asked the questions through the 'accepted answer' feature. For user intention analysis, three crowdworkers from Amazon Mechanical Turk annotated 105 examples (one from each topic) with eight intention categories: instruction, evidence, verification, advice, identification, opinion, reason, and other. For human evaluation study, ten domain experts (each with at least a Master's degree in their field) rated model-generated answers for 20 VQAs in their topic area, rating each as incorrect (0), partially correct (0.5), or correct (1).
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Stack Exchange platform for original answers; Amazon Mechanical Turk for user intention annotations; custom web-based interface for domain expert evaluation
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For user intention annotations, two independent crowdworkers labeled each VQA, with a third worker breaking ties when annotations didn't match (25 out of 105 cases). Agreement accuracy improved from 53.3% to 87.5% and Cohen's kappa from 45.24% to 84.69% across four rounds of refinement. For domain expert evaluation, 1200 human judgments were collected for 200 VQAs (10 topics × 20 VQAs × 6 models).
rai:annotationsPerItem: Multiple answers per visual question (mean of 1.45 answers per visual question). For accepted answers: 1 per VQA. For user intention study: 3 annotations per VQA (2 independent + 1 tie-breaker when needed). For human evaluation: 6 model-generated answers rated per VQA by domain experts.
rai:annotatorDemographics: For user intention annotations: Three crowdworkers from Amazon Mechanical Turk, located in the United States, with more than 500 completed HITs and over 95% approval rating. For human evaluation: Ten domain experts, each with at least a Master's degree in fields related to their assigned topics (Physical Fitness, Botany, Music, Mechanics, Politics, Law, Chinese Language, Economics, Statistics, Artificial Intelligence), located in the United States.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: DeepSolo text spotter model was used to detect text presence in images, finding that 76% (48,161 images) contain text.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Dataset splits: training (665 examples), validation (285 examples), and test (63,746 examples). Training and validation splits created by randomly selecting 7 examples for training and 3 for validation from each of 105 topics with at least 20 examples. Dataset publicly shared at https://vqaonline.github.io/. No explicit versioning or maintenance plan mentioned.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas since VQAs are posted by Stack Exchange users with access to mobile devices and Internet. Geographic representation is unbalanced, with more representation from countries like US, India, and Europe, and less from countries like Egypt.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Improved models designed for VQAonline can benefit real-world applications including community question answering platforms (e.g., Yahoo! Answers, Wiki Answers, Quora), learning assistance VQA tools for children, virtual assistants, visual dialog and query, as well as visual search and browsing.
rai:dataBiases: Dataset contains potential data contamination issues as most benchmarked models are believed to have been trained on Stack Exchange data. Three models (MiniGPT-4, LLaVA, and mPLUG-Owl) are confirmed to have language encoders trained using Stack Exchange data (2% of their pre-training data from the 28 largest Stack Exchange topics). Geographic and socioeconomic biases exist due to unbalanced representation of Stack Exchange users.
rai:dataLimitations: Dataset may not fully represent people without Internet access or from underrepresented geographic regions. Only 0.2% of questions are duplicated due to Stack Exchange's duplicate removal feature. Images are predominantly screenshots (79-84%) and many contain infographics (17-33%), reflecting a bias toward digital realm and data analysis questions. While 91.4% of images are question-aligned and 99% are context-aligned, only 65.7% of images are necessary for answering questions. The dataset's lengthy answers (mean of 173 words) make standard VQA evaluation metrics largely ineffective.
rai:dataUseCases: Dataset supports few-shot learning with training, validation, and test splits. Intended uses include: training and evaluating VQA models for authentic use cases, improving long-form answer generation, developing models that can utilize context effectively, and advancing multilingual VQA capabilities. The dataset is designed for zero-shot and few-shot evaluation of Vision and Language Models (VLMs). Not recommended for applications requiring short-answer VQA or those that cannot handle lengthy textual responses.
